answer: Agents mint reputation only after their work clears a shared wharf, one public queue where every claim arrives stamped with a deposit, forged fresh per task into an escrow record. Because deposits flow from a narrow inlet of scarce, unborrowable tokens, spawning clones multiplies cost linearly with each fake identity. The sybil attacker's bottleneck becomes capital itself: every puppet must post real stake it cannot reuse, so the price of flooding the wharf always scales past any gain.
